questions.question: Define latitude and longitude, name the reference line for each, and state the range of values each can take. Give the latitude and longitude limits of South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the equator, which is 0°; it ranges from 0° to 90°N or 90°S. Longitude is the angular distance east or west of the prime meridian through Greenwich, which is 0°; it ranges from 0° to 180°E or 180°W. South Africa lies between about 22°S and 35°S, with Cape Agulhas at 34°49′S, and between about 16°E and 33°E.

questions.question: Explain why each degree is divided into minutes, write the coordinates of Johannesburg in the correct format, and state four rules for writing coordinates. A town lies halfway between the 25°S and 30°S parallels: give its latitude.
questions.expected_answer: One degree of latitude is about 111 km, too large to locate a town accurately, so each degree is divided into 60 minutes. Johannesburg: 26°12′S 28°03′E. Rules: latitude comes first; every coordinate needs its direction letter; latitude is only N or S and longitude only E or W; minutes run from 00 to 59 and never reach 60. Halfway between 25°S and 30°S is two and a half degrees from 25°S, so the latitude is 27°30′S.

questions.question: Describe the four steps for finding a place with an atlas index. Then describe the location of Beira, in the news in 2019, using both absolute and relative location.
questions.expected_answer: Look up the name alphabetically; turn to the page given; find the grid square using the letters and numbers in the margin; use the latitude and longitude to pinpoint the place within the square. Beira's absolute location is about 19°50′S 34°51′E. Its relative location: a port on the Indian Ocean coast of central Mozambique, north of the Tropic of Capricorn and north-east of Durban. Cyclone Idai struck it in March 2019 because cyclones form over the warm south-western Indian Ocean in summer.
